analysis: The PR adds a coordinator-side cold KV-per-token forecast. coldKVEstimatesLocked (cold_kv_estimate.go) builds operation-local estimates as the MAX of KVBytesPerToken from peer providers that hold the same (model, WeightHash, version, metallib) key. The rate is capped at MaxBytesPerToken. The peer must be routing-eligible, have a fresh capacity report, use the mlx-swift backend, and have verified runtime, manifest and metallib. The rate is applied to cold providers in autopilot_snapshot.go (ColdTokenBudget), in first_content_plan.go via snapshotProviderIntoPLockedEx(..., estimates), and in fleet_sample.go diagnostics. admission/memory.go adds Memory.KVBytesPerToken and falls back to the 400k default when it is <=0. The defined security-relevant weakness is that the rate and artifact identity are self-reported (WeightHash is fail-open), so one malicious eligible provider can steer other providers' admission and fit (reported as a finding). The lock order looks consistent: r.mu is held, p.mu is taken per provider, and no p.mu is held on entry. There are no authorization, attestation or encryption changes. Not reviewed: the definitions of fleetSampleColdKVEstimates, snapshotProviderIntoPLockedEx and its other callers (registry routing and commitProviderReservation), the kvbudget.ClampRate bounds, and how Memory.KVBytesPerToken is populated, because those hunks are not in the supplied patches. The extra O(models x providers) work per reservation scan under r.mu.RLock is a possible latency concern.

findings.detail: observedColdKVRateLocked takes KVBytesPerToken from any routing-eligible peer's self-reported capacity slot. coldKVEstimatesLocked then takes the MAX across peers and applies it as the cold-model KV estimate for every other provider with the same key (model, WeightHash, version, metallib). WeightHash and PromptWorkIdentity.ModelArtifactHash are provider-supplied, and weight-hash enforcement is fail-open (TB-002/SEC-007). A malicious but eligible provider can therefore advertise a loaded slot with an inflated rate up to kvbudget.MaxBytesPerToken, after copying a competitor's artifact hash. Competitors' cold KV budget in MemoryAdmits and autopilot ColdTokenBudget is then overstated, so they are wrongly rejected for larger requests or lose autopilot fit and routing share. A single peer with an unrealistically low rate can instead create an under-estimate, since only >0 is checked, with no lower bound or plausibility check against model/hardware. The under-estimate over-admits or mis-plans loads. Destination gates remain authoritative, so impact is bounded to routing/availability manipulation. Fix: do not accept a peer rate from a single provider. Require corroboration from several distinct accounts or machines, or derive the rate from catalog/structural model metadata. Clamp to a plausible range for the model, and use a median or quorum instead of the max.
findings.title: Peer-reported KV rate drives other providers' cold admission and autopilot fit, keyed only on self-reported identifiers
